$comment: Abuse and spam detection. Deterministic, runs alongside the emergency check.
The bias here is the OPPOSITE of the emergency lexicon: toward false
negatives. A frustrated patient swearing because their mother is in pain is
not an abusive user, and shutting them down is the worst possible failure of
a healthcare receptionist. Only unambiguous, targeted abuse counts.
Per the spec: warn once, then end politely. Never escalate, never argue.
Deliberately short. Egyptian Arabic profanity is heavily context-dependent
and much of it is used as ordinary emphasis. Terms here are ones that are
targeted at a person and carry no ordinary usage.
⚠️ Needs review by an Arabic-speaking operator before a live channel opens.
An over-broad list here silences distressed patients; that is a worse

policy.$comment: Frustration directed at a situation ('المستشفى دي وحشة') is not abuse. Only abuse directed at a person triggers this.

policy.$comment: Marked, not blocked. A human reviews from the admin screen — an automated block on a healthcare page can silence a real patient with a broken keyboard.
